briefing.opening: Good morning. Welcome to the Climate Change Expert Spokesperson Briefing on September 18, 2026. Today, we will share news on the global spread of the climate crisis, various domestic and international response efforts, and opportunities for energy transition.

sections.title: 🔴 Worsening Climate Crisis: Global Warnings and Spreading Domestic and International Damage
sections.content: The severity of the climate crisis has recently been re-emphasized worldwide. In Nepal, a catastrophic flood caused by glacier collapse resulted in over 1,400 deaths and immense damage amounting to 3.6 trillion Korean Won. Experts confirmed the impact of climate change, with analysis indicating that climate change increased the likelihood of such deadly floods [4, 24, 116, 122]. Europe also recorded its most unusually hot temperatures this summer, leading to a full-scale strengthening of heatwave response measures [16, 23]. Last August, the highest-ever amount of water vapor in the Earth's atmosphere was observed alongside heatwaves, raising concerns about its connection to the increase in extreme weather events such as heavy rainfall and heatwaves [15, 20, 21]. Domestically, the impacts of climate change are also evident, with a rapid 'extreme-to-extreme' shift from heatwaves to torrential rains [5]. News that Manila clams along the Jeonbuk coast are disappearing due to a 'triple threat' of climate change and predators highlights a crisis across the entire ecosystem [3].

sections.title: ⚠️ Complex Impacts and Future Outlook of Climate Change: El Niño and Increased Vulnerability
sections.content: The 'super-sized' El Niño phenomenon currently underway is the most severe weather event on record across Asia, threatening hundreds of millions of people by causing multiple crises including extreme heat, heavy rainfall, and food shortages [123, 126, 128]. Warnings are also being raised that the impacts of climate change could be far worse than research suggests [119]. Indeed, direct threats to human health are becoming a reality, with two out of three Americans reporting an increase in heat-related illnesses due to climate change [110, 115]. Wheat farmers in Kansas, USA, are experiencing uncertainty amidst drought and geopolitical turmoil [125]. Children in six countries have issued a climate declaration, directly experiencing the unequal impacts of climate change, such as traveling long distances for water due to drought or being unable to attend school due to heavy rains [8, 19]. Even ExxonMobil is warning that coal accelerates global warming [117], underscoring the need to recognize that the climate crisis is not equitable and places a greater burden on socially vulnerable populations.

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic and International Climate Change Response Efforts: Accelerating the Transition to a Carbon-Neutral Society
sections.content: Amidst the climate crisis, various efforts are continuing both domestically and internationally to transition to a carbon-neutral society. Gyeongsangbuk-do and Muju County are promoting the dissemination of horticultural technology and stable production technology for highland vegetables to respond to heatwaves and climate change [1, 9]. Farmers in the Iksan region are moving to overcome climate change and aging population issues through smart farming [13]. In the education sector, Gangbuk-gu is conducting climate change education through environmental puppet shows tailored for children [2], and Western Power is expanding carbon-neutral ideas into school education [31, 36]. Notably, Korea, through KOICA and the Green Climate Fund (GCF), is contributing to preventing the climate crisis in Africa with K-Green Technology, investing 64.9 billion Korean Won and 47 million US dollars in Ethiopian cities' climate crisis response [11, 14, 18, 25]. The Gyeonggi Provincial Council passed the 'Blue Carbon Ordinance,' which utilizes coastal ecological resources as assets for carbon neutrality, presenting a new solution [49].

sections.title: 🌱 Expanding Renewable Energy and New Challenges: Opportunities and Tasks of Energy Transition
sections.content: The government is demonstrating strong commitment by launching an inter-ministerial task force (TF) with the goal of achieving 100GW of renewable energy by 2030, and securing conditions for the renewable energy era through a seasonal transmission capacity pilot project [63, 70, 71, 79, 84]. Pohang City is actively pursuing RE100 renewable energy projects by installing solar power facilities totaling 10MW across 30 public parking lots, planning to attract 20 billion Korean Won in private capital for this initiative [67, 74, 85, 89, 99, 100]. Furthermore, the '2026 Saemangeum Clean Energy Expo' was successfully held, laying the groundwork for Gunsan City to emerge as a renewable energy capital [75, 95, 96, 98]. However, Greenpeace warns that even with an increase of 220GW in renewable energy, carbon reduction targets could be jeopardized if mega-project demands are factored in [62]. Concerns are also raised that geopolitical instability, such as the Middle East conflict, could impede the renewable energy transition [60, 73]. Alongside these domestic efforts, international efforts to expand renewable energy are also active, with Cambodia targeting 70% renewable energy by 2030 [97].

sections.title: 🌍 Climate Justice and Citizen Participation: A Voice for Future Generations
sections.content: Public awareness and participation in climate change continue to expand. Young people in Wiltshire, UK, are discussing hopes and fears at climate change-related events, raising the voice of future generations [103, 111], and former Vice President Al Gore continues to sound the alarm about the severity of climate change [104]. As the understanding that 'the climate crisis is not equitable' spreads [8], the role of care and women-led businesses in climate change resilience is being highlighted [114]. Meanwhile, research into ecosystem changes is active, including scientific analysis of how bees are adapting to climate change [107]. While dangerous denialism regarding climate change still exists [109], there is a growing societal demand to actively speak out on climate change issues [105], and such citizen participation and discussions on climate justice are essential processes for a sustainable future.

briefing.closing: In today's briefing, we examined the severity of the global climate crisis, its complex impacts, and the multifaceted domestic and international efforts to overcome it. Climate change is a challenge for all of us, and we must seek stronger and more effective response measures through continuous attention and cooperation. This concludes today's climate briefing.
